{"content": "## Creating a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance with an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and Ubuntu 20.04 LTS

Below you’ll find two ways to create the instance:

1. **Using the `gcloud` CLI** – the easiest and most common method.
2. **Using the REST API (curl)** – useful if you want to embed the call in a script or a CI/CD pipeline.

Both examples assume you already have:
- A Google Cloud project with billing enabled.
- The Compute Engine API enabled.
- The `gcloud` CLI installed and authenticated (`gcloud auth login`).
- Sufficient GPU quota for the `nvidia-a6000` accelerator in the chosen zone.

---

### 1. `gcloud` CLI command

```bash
# Variables – replace with your own values
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"          # choose a zone that supports RTX A6000
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"  # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM – adjust as needed
GPU_COUNT=1
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-a6000"
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"

# Create the instance

gcloud compute instances create $INSTANCE_NAME \
  --project=$PROJECT_ID \
  --zone=$ZONE \
  --machine-type=$MACHINE_TYPE \
  --accelerator=type=$GPU_TYPE,count=$GPU_COUNT \
  --image-family=$IMAGE_FAMILY \
  --image-project=$IMAGE_PROJECT \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --metadata startup-script='#!/bin/bash
# Install NVIDIA drivers
apt-get update
apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535
# Verify installation
nvidia-smi' \
  --tags=http-server,https-server \
  --service-account=default \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform
```

**Explanation of key flags**:
- `--accelerator`: attaches the RTX A6000 GPU.
- `--image-family` & `--image-project`: pulls the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image.
- `--boot-disk-size` & `--boot-disk-type`: SSD for better I/O performance.
- `--metadata startup-script`: runs a shell script on first boot to install the NVIDIA driver.
- `--tags`: optional, useful if you want to expose HTTP/HTTPS ports.
- `--service-account` & `--scopes`: give the instance full Cloud Platform access.

After the instance starts, you can SSH into it and run `nvidia-smi` to confirm the GPU is visible.

---

### 2. REST API call (curl)

```bash
# Get an OAuth 2.0 access token (requires gcloud auth application-default)
ACCESS_TOKEN=$(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)

# Variables – replace with your own values
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"
GPU_COUNT=1
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-a6000"
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"

# Construct the JSON body
read -r -d '' INSTANCE_JSON <<EOF
{
  "name": "$INSTANCE_NAME",
  "machineType": "zones/$ZONE/machineTypes/$MACHINE_TYPE",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/$IMAGE_PROJECT/global/images/family/$IMAGE_FAMILY",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/$PROJECT_ID/zones/$ZONE/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/$PROJECT_ID/zones/$ZONE/acceleratorTypes/$GPU_TYPE",
      "acceleratorCount": $GPU_COUNT
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        {"type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT"}
      ]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535\nnvidia-smi"
      }
    ]
  },
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default@${PROJECT_ID}.iam.gserviceaccount.com",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  }
}
EOF

# Make the API request
curl -X POST "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/zones/$ZONE/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "$INSTANCE_JSON"
```

**Notes**:
- The `acceleratorType` URL uses the project‑zone‑accelerator format. For RTX A6000, the accelerator type is `nvidia-a6000`.
- The `startup-script` installs the NVIDIA driver automatically.
- Ensure you have the `compute.instances.create` permission and sufficient GPU quota.

---

### Quick Checklist

| Step | Action |
|------|--------|
| 1 | Enable Compute Engine API and GPU quota for `nvidia-a6000`. |
| 2 | Choose a zone that supports RTX A6000 (e.g., `us-central1-a`, `europe-west4-a`). |
| 3 | Decide on machine type (CPU + RAM). |
| 4 | Use either `gcloud` command or REST API to create the instance. |
| 5 | Verify GPU visibility with `nvidia-smi`. |

Happy GPU computing!", "filename": "create-rtx-a6000-instance.md"}

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, with a default value that allows for a reasonable amount of time for most web pages to load.

user_agent.description: The User-Agent string to be used for the HTTP request to simulate a particular browser, which is optional. Some websites may require this for access.
